0.content:
Astromancer Barbeloth Trismegistus, a seer-witch of the Hexenzirkel known by the codename B, is Mona's master. She taught Mona hydromancy, which Mona calls the one true success of the old woman's research. On taking Mona as a pupil she renamed her "Megistus" and renamed herself "Trismegistus", "thrice as great". She also gave Mona a Vision-shaped teaching aid: "May your heart of truth be with you." Mona's own Hydro Vision later appeared within it, and it is the only keepsake of their time together. Barbeloth used to chase Mona around while Mona tried to distract her with a Hydro phantom, and she nicknamed her "Meg". Mona insults her constantly ("old hag", "stubborn dimwit", "batty old lady") and defends her art fiercely.

Mona has not gone back since reading the diary, and the two now communicate only by letter. In 6.2 Barbeloth sent a book with three letters: an affectionate memory, a ritual for the Sign of Truth at the gate of Khaenri'ah, and a third letter that laughed at Mona for actually trying it. It went on to explain why the site was safe and then boasted for thousands of words. Paimon observed that the two quarrel over sentimental things and get emotional over dry academic ones.

In Simulanka (4.8, limited) Mona found a statue of her master's younger self as the Goddess of Prophecy and refused to believe the old hag ever looked like that. Then she remembered the "fashionista phase" in the diary. Studying the world's starscape, she conceded quietly that her master deserves the title Trismegistus after all. In 3.5 (limited) she felt someone watching her at the Hexenzirkel's sky island and suspected her master, only to find Alice imitating Barbeloth's voice.

1.comment: Mona: The Diary and the Fifty-Year Pact
1.content:
Fifty years ago Barbeloth made a pact with Alice, and Alice kept a confidential box of Barbeloth's. As her master grew less spry, Mona was sent to fetch it from Alice's "successor", with a warning that she would regret looking inside. Mona hoped to beat the successor in a contest of arts and so prove herself superior to her own master. She brought the Traveler along as a pretend disciple. The successor turned out to be Klee, who knew only how to make bombs and had buried the box at Windrise with her treasures. While the others dug it up, Mona leafed through a "ridiculous diary" that had fallen out of Klee's backpack. It was the box's real contents: her master's diary from fifty years ago, "the dark history of her youth". Convinced astrology would expose any lie and that her master would tear her to shreds, Mona decided to stay in Mondstadt until "the old crone" reached the end of her days.

In the 6.4 event (limited) Varka and Nicole told her every Hexenzirkel mage knows the story (except, Nicole added, Rhinedottir). Mona was mortified, then hoped aloud that the old hag would not come to Mondstadt to settle the score.

2.content:
Mona's astrology is hydromancy: reading the stars' illusory reflection in water. The night sky shows people's fate, and its inverted reflection reveals the truth. She uses a scryglass and still water, works best in clear weather and with pure snowmelt, and says heavy rain hazes her scryglass. She believes the stars of a constellation are real bodies in deep space. Vision bearers' constellations map their whole destiny. Her rules: never use astrology for Mora or mundane problems, or the starry ether forsakes the astrologer. State results, never advise. Do not read your own fate. Her only stable income is The Steambird's "All Things Astrological" column, which she turned into dense, footnoted scholarship that readers love without understanding.

In 2.8 (limited) her mirage showed her lesson. Once she thought she understood all fates, lost her way, and "couldn't see the stars any longer". Her master's warning was that if an astrologist becomes confused, not even astrology can help. She concluded that observing fate is enough and there is no need to force it to change, and then spoke of seizing her own destiny.

3.content:
Klee is the daughter of Alice, her master's lifelong rival, so Mona expected a successor to great knowledge. Klee asked whether the "ocean of stars" had fish in it. Klee later fled when Mona learned what was in the box. Mona now visits Klee and Albedo, mostly for a free meal and secondly to trade ideas with Albedo, a fellow student of a famous master. Klee says she loves it when Mona comes round, even though she understands little of what Mona says. Mona envies Albedo's freedom to research without mundane worries. He once asked whether her master was illustrious or a "stubborn dimwit". After real thought she answered that the techniques were exceptional but she has surpassed her master in knowing the price of eggs, butter and wheat.

Mona says Klee's constellation, Trifolium, means luck, which she slightly envies. Then again, with luck she might never have met the old woman. During Windblume (3.5, limited) Klee told her that Barbeloth had helped choose her hat. By 6.4 Mona said that she knows Klee did not mean to cause her trouble.

4.content:
Mona waited outside Liyue Harbor for the Traveler, having foreseen the meeting, and greeted them with "You're not from this world, are you?" She offered a reading of their fate, "even regarding such distant and foggy matters as gods and kin", in exchange for playing her disciple. She found the Traveler's fate a fog to Teyvat's stars. She has never managed the reading, though she said she was running tests. She tells the Traveler that their journey is far from over. She breaks her rule against advice for them, because their fates were intertwined from the beginning. She cannot read Paimon's origins either.

She thinks the Traveler cooks remarkably well: the Golden Crab they made her at Wangshu Inn was the most delicious thing she had eaten in ages. In the Serenitea Pot she half-fears she will never adjust to paying rent again. In Fontaine (4.2) she comforted them: astrology is rational but fate may not be. It is cruel but can be beautiful, and she still hopes for miracles. She thinks they always meet by coincidence because both of them help those who are struggling.

5.content: When a Fatui Harbinger stalked the Traveler, Mona recognised him at once ("any junior fortune-teller" could have) and whisked everyone away in a Hydro bubble. Scaramouche wondered how she knew. At Musk Reef he announced that the stars and sky are a gigantic lie, called them suckers and left. Furious ("No one disrespects me!"), Mona tore through his subordinates. Afterwards she wondered whether the "false sky" she was taught to mention in readings meant more than she had thought.

6.content: Mona's home is a former magic laboratory at the southern end of Mondstadt City, beyond Schulz's blacksmith. Someone had sealed it with Hydro magic; the Guild's specialists who might have broken it were not interested, and Mona judged it nigh impossible to force. Mona broke the seal with astrology, and its owner Goth gratefully offered to rent it to her "at the lowest possible price". She had assumed it would be free, but took it rather than be homeless. In the commission "Owe Mora, Pay Mora" (2.4) she is late with rent because she has paid a deposit on a Fontaine celestial globe. She scrapes the rent together and lives on salad for days. The inside is crammed with expensive books (one tagged at 990,000 Mora) and instruments. She insists she is "occasionally out of Mora", not a pauper.

7.content: During Windblume's Breath (3.5, limited) she answered the last part of the Hexenzirkel's lantern prophecy at their sky island: there is no tale more befitting "a legend that never ends" than human fates. She marvelled that so many mysterious women all know each other. In 6.4 (limited) Alice hired her for several roles in a memory bubble. Mona praised the pay, saying the Hexenzirkel never promises an amount it cannot deliver.

8.content: The mirage also recreated her own overstuffed laboratory, to her horror. Fischl recalled treating her to dinner with her parents, and Mona praised Fischl's mother's stew and cold cuts.

9.content: Mona was in Fontaine at The Steambird's invitation to speak as an astrologist on a panel about the prophecy. She warned the Traveler away from strange water and explained the name Megistus. She said she was born in Mondstadt and her parents moved to Dornman Port, so she was not at risk of dissolving. She agreed to ask her master about the prophecy but could not reach her. At the panel she backed Charlotte's view that people should prepare their own rescue rather than wait for the end, and let no prophecy commandeer their lives. When the Traveler described N's visit she was astonished. She then admitted she had meant to stay out of it, but could not.

key: A Dry Well Doth Not Reflect the Stars
10.content: In Mona's Witch's Homework quest the Traveler brought her a book from her master. Three letters fell out. Barbeloth said lakes in Khaenri'ah reflected the true stars because a "Sign of Truth" (the Sign of Apaosha) formed in water can bypass the false sky to the outer universe. Only past the false sky can one measure the cosmic parameters needed to predict a world's fate. Her task was to open a Sign at the gate of Khaenri'ah in Sumeru. Mona grudgingly admitted the parameters might work, and that it saved her a night's lodging, and performed the invocation. It opened just long enough for Abyssal Tenebrous Mimesis to come through, and it showed her none of the true stars. She fought them, testing her improved hydromancy. The third letter laughed at her for trying, explained that the unstable, hidden site kept any failure small-scale, and boasted of the new theory and the Scryglass's practical use. Mona cut it off there.

11.comment: Mona: Homeward and the True Moon (6.4)
11.content: In a limited-time 6.4 event Mona played two Fatui parts in Alice's memory-bubble re-enactment, because "the more roles you play, the more you get paid". She posed a riddle about not doubting one's eyes or the ground beneath one's feet. Then she haggled over a crest for hundreds of thousands of Mora, fighting as a Mirror Maiden if negotiations failed. Afterwards she said she had seen in her scryglass that the Traveler had reeled in the true moon from beyond the false firmament. She wonders what hydromancy would show if it reflected the true moon instead of the false stars, and is taking odd jobs to fund the equipment. When Varka suggested she just contact Barbeloth, she accused him of doing it on purpose.

12.content: Mona dismisses Venti as the bard who does nothing all day. When she tried to scry him, she could see nothing. A wind came up that she could not open her eyes against, tearing at her hat and clothes, and she swore never to try again. She does not know why. Venti, for his part, jokes that fortune-telling and singing both leave you too broke to buy a drink, and that both are cultural traditions with value.

13.content: Mona reads people through their constellations. Jean (Leo Minor): strength and responsibility shouldered too young; a lioness who will return to lead her pride. Kaeya (Pavo Ocellus): grandeur hiding ugly realities behind charm. He believes he has broken with his past, but fate will catch up with him and force a major decision. Diluc (Noctua): a lone guardian keeping watch in the night, longing for the dawn yet destined to solitude in the dark days before it arrives, "or maybe Noctua's the one tied to wealth". Lisa (Tempus Fugit): knowledge traded against time, like sand that, once it stops, stays still, or rather "becomes lazy". Klee (Trifolium): good luck.

14.content: When the witch-hunter Prune came to Mondstadt, Alice had told her that Witch B's name was "Megistus", leaving off the "Tris". Prune decided Mona, with her big pointy hat, was B, and tried to confront her publicly. Prune admits she harassed her a bit and blames Alice. Mona accepted her apology.
